# Introduction to causal inference

## Background: What is causal inference?

```{r out.width=".9\\textwidth", results="asis", echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("img/causal_inference_two.pdf")
```

## The Nobel Prize 2021 in Economic Sciences

```{r out.width=".4\\linewidth", results="asis", echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("img/nobelprize_card_angrist_imbens-3_2-992x656.jpg")
```

$$
\textsf{David Card}, \underbrace{\textsf{\color{blue} Joshua Angrist}}_{\textsf{instrumental variable}}, \underbrace{\textsf{\color{blue} Guido Imbens}}_{\textsf{matching, propensity}}
$$

> "For the methodological contributions to the analysis of causal relationships"

\tiny
`https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2021`



## The goal of causal effect inference

\large

\begin{enumerate}
\item<1-> Instead of \textbf{\color{teal} "seeing"} what happened (data analysis), we want to measure \textbf{\color{magenta} the effect of "doing"} an experiment (intervention).
\item<2-> Because correlation is not causation.
\item<3> If it is not causation, then what is it?
\end{enumerate}

## Common misconception - correlation implies causation

:::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=.8}

\Large

Henry Niles also wrote, *"To contrast 'causation' and 'correlation' is unwarranted \textbf{\color{magenta} because causation is simply perfect correlation}"*

:::
::: {.column width=.2}

```{r out.width="\\linewidth", results="asis", echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("img/munch_the_scream.jpg")
```

:::
::::::

\vfill

\small
Pearl, *The Book of Why*, p.78

- How do we measure causal effects? Will any experiment do?

## A working example: Why correlation is not causation

\large

* $U_{i}$: The age at which a person $i$ enrolled in this study.

* $X_{i}$: An indicator variable for whether a physician decided to administer this new preventative drug ($X_{i}=1$) or not ($X_{i}=0$).

* $Y_{i}$: Biomarker protein concentration (e.g., Amyloid-beta protein disrupts normal brain functions).

\normalsize

## A hypothetical data generating scheme

\large

* A person $i$'s age $U_{i}$.

\large

1. Prescribe the preventative drug based on the subject's age $U_{i}$ (as they might need one):

$$
P(X_{i}=1|U_{i}) = \sigma \left( U_{i} \delta \right)
$$

2. A biomarker protein concentration:

$$\mathbb{E}\!\left[ Y_{i}\middle| X, U \right] =  X_{i} \tau + U_{i} \beta$$


## **Recap**: Directed Acyclic Graph

```{r out.width=".4\\textwidth", results="asis", echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("img/causalDAG/DAG_x_to_z_to_y.pdf")
```

$$p(X,Y,Z) =
\underset{\textsf{\color{blue}first edge}}{p(Y|X)}\quad
\underset{\textsf{\color{magenta}second edge}}{p(Z|Y)}\quad
\underset{\textsf{\color{teal}first node}}{p(X)}$$

## DAG: Causal path/trail and reachability

```{r out.width=".4\\textwidth", results="asis", echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("img/causalDAG/DAG_x_to_z_to_y.pdf")
```

* There is a path between $X$ and $Y$

* Also between $Y$ and $Z$

* Also from $X$ to $Z$

## DAG: Conditioning (and/or adjustment)

```{r out.width=".4\\textwidth", results="asis", echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("img/causalDAG/DAG_x_to_z_to_y_cond.pdf")
```

* A shaded node = conditioning like $P(Z|Y=y^\star)$ and $P(Y=y^\star|X)$

* There is a path between $X$ and $Y$

* Also between $Y$ and $Z$

* **But** no path from $X$ to $Z$

## d-separation: testing conditional independence (flow vs. no flow)

\normalsize

:::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=.3}

```{r include=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
.add.fig <- function(x) {
    knitr::include_graphics("img/backdoor_exercise/" %&% x %&% ".pdf")
}
```

```{r out.width=".8\\linewidth", results="asis", onslide.plot="1-", echo=FALSE}
.add.fig("dag_x_y_z_1")
```

```{r out.width=".8\\linewidth", results="asis", onslide.plot="4-", echo=FALSE}
.add.fig("dag_x_y_z_1_block")
```

\vfill

\only<1-3>{
\textbf{\color{teal} Flow}: The outcome of $Z$ depends on the effect of X
}
\only<4->{
\textbf{\color{orange} No} \textbf{\color{teal} Flow}: The outcome of $Z$ solely depends on $Y=y^*$, not $X$
}

:::
::: {.column width=.3}

```{r out.width=".8\\linewidth", results="asis", onslide.plot="2-", echo=FALSE}
## X <- Y -> Z
.add.fig("dag_x_y_z_2")
```

```{r out.width=".8\\linewidth", results="asis", onslide.plot="5-", echo=FALSE}
## X <- Y -> Z
.add.fig("dag_x_y_z_2_block")
```

\vfill

\only<2-3>{
\textbf{\color{teal} Flow}: The outcome of $Z$ depends on the effect of $Y$; so does the outcome of $X$ on that of $Y$
}
\only<5->{
\textbf{\color{orange} No} \textbf{\color{teal} Flow}: The outcome of $Z$ solely depends on $Y=y^*$, not $X$
}

:::
::: {.column width=.3}

```{r out.width=".8\\linewidth", results="asis", onslide.plot="3-", echo=FALSE}
## X -> Y <- Z
.add.fig("dag_x_y_z_3")
```

```{r out.width=".8\\linewidth", results="asis", only.plot="6", echo=FALSE}
## X -> Y <- Z
.add.fig("dag_x_y_z_3_block")
```

\only<7>{
\textbf{\color{teal} Flow}: deeper v-structure
}

```{r out.width=".8\\linewidth", results="asis", only.plot="7", echo=FALSE}
## X -> Y <- Z
.add.fig("dag_x_y_z_3_deep")
```

\vfill

\only<3>{
\textbf{\color{orange} No} \textbf{\color{teal} Flow}: The outcome of $Z$ only affects $Y$; so does $X$
}
\only<6>{
\textbf{\color{teal} Flow}: The observed outcome $Y=y^*$ could stem from $X$ or/and $Z$
}

:::
::::::


## Going back to the same working example

:::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=.45}

```{r}
set.seed(1)
```

```{r sim_1, echo = T, echo=FALSE}
## Simulation parameters
n = 200; .delta = 2; .tau = -1; .beta = 2; .eps = .3
sgm <- function(x) 1/(1+ exp(-x))

## A generative scheme
uu <- rnorm(n) # standardised age
xx <- rbinom(n=n, size=1, prob=sgm(uu * .delta))
yy <- xx * .tau + uu * .beta + rnorm(n) * .eps
```

${}$

**If there were** no confounding:

```{r echo=T}
yy.unc <- xx * .tau + rnorm(n) * .eps
```

:::
::: {.column width=.55}

$${}$$

* The variable $U$ confounds $X$ and $Y$.

* How can we represent it graphically?


```{r out.width=".4\\linewidth", results="asis", only.plot="3-4", echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("img/DAG_confounded.pdf")
```

```{r out.width=".4\\linewidth", results="asis", only.plot="5", echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("img/DAG_confounded_backdoor.pdf")
```

\begin{enumerate}
\item<3-> How can we identify the causal effect, $X{\to}Y$?
\item<4-> Why can't we just report the correlation/association between $X$ and $Y$?
\end{enumerate}

:::
::::::

## Differential biomarker analysis suggests that our drug can exacerbate AD

<!-- $$ -->
<!-- P(X_{i} | U_{i}) = \frac{1}{1 + \exp\left( U_{i} \beta \right)} -->
<!-- $$ -->

```{r echo=F}
## Propensity scores
## estimated by
## a logistic
## regression model
e.hat <-
  glm(xx~uu,
      family="binomial") %>%
  predict %>%
  sgm
```

```{r echo = F}
## Treatment assignment variable
x.f <- factor(xx, c(0,1), c("untreated", "treated"))

.df <- tibble(x = x.f,
              u = uu,
              y = yy,
              y.unc = yy.unc,
              e = e.hat)
```

```{r echo = FALSE, fig.width=3, fig.height=2.5, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(.df, aes(x, y))+
  geom_violin(fill = "gray") +
  geom_boxplot(width = .25) +
  ylab("Amyloid beta (Y)") +
  xlab("Drug treated (X)")
```

## Back to the AD example: Can we save the study?

If there is any systematic bias, we should adjust for it.

```{r show_sim_data_1_w, echo=FALSE, fig.width=5.5, fig.height=2}
p1 <-
  ggplot(.df, aes(u, x))+
  geom_jitter(height=.1) +
  xlab("U (standardised age)") +
  ylab("X (treatment assignment)")

p2 <-
  ggplot(.df, aes(u, e))+
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(se=FALSE, colour="red", formula="y ~ x", method="loess") +
  xlab("U (standardised age)") +
  ylab("Propensity: P(X=1|U)")

wrap_plots(p1, p2, nrow = 1, widths=c(3,4))
```

## Inverse Propensity Weighting reverses confounding

:::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=.5}

```{r out.width=".8\\linewidth", results="asis", only.plot="1", echo=FALSE}
knitr::include_graphics("img/DAG_confounded_backdoor_controlled.pdf")
```

\only<2->{
$$\hat{Y}_{i}^{(1)} = \frac{X_{i} Y_{i}}{\hat{p}(X_{i}=1|U_{i})}$$

$$\hat{Y}_{i}^{(0)} = \frac{(1-X_{i}) Y_{i}}{1 - \hat{p}(X_{i}=1|U_{i})}$$
}

\only<3>{
equivalently give weights for $\forall$ i
$$
W_{i} \propto \left\{ \begin{array}{l l}
1/\hat{p}(X_{i}=1|U_{i}) & X_{i} = 1\\
1/\hat{p}(X_{i}=0|U_{i}) & X_{i} = 0\\
\end{array}
\right.
$$
}

:::
::: {.column width=.5}

```{r echo = F}
sigmoid <- function(x) 1/(1+exp(-x))
clamp <- function(x, lb = .1, ub = .9)
    pmin(pmax(x, lb), ub)
```

```{r echo = F}
x <- as.integer(.df$x == "treated")
y <- .df$y
u <- .df$u
```

```{r echo=TRUE}
p.xu <-
    glm(x~u, family="binomial") %>%
    predict() %>%
    sigmoid() %>%
    clamp() # avoid strict 0/1

ww <- x / p.xu + (1-x) / (1-p.xu)
```

${}$

**Propensity**: Pr. of assignment $X=1$:

$$\log\frac{\bf\color{magenta} p(X|U)}{1-{\bf\color{magenta} p(X|U)}} \approx \beta_{0} + \beta_{1} U$$

:::
::::::


## Take samples inversely proportional to propensity

```{r include = F}
.df$w <- ww
```

:::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=.4}

```{r fig.width=2.5, fig.height=2.5, onslide.plot="1-", echo=FALSE}

```

:::
::: {.column width=.6}

```{r fig.width=3.5, fig.height=2.5, onslide.plot="2", echo=FALSE}
ggplot(.df, aes(x,y,size=w))+
    geom_jitter(height=0, width=.1, alpha=.5) +
```

## If we bootstrap (sample with replacement)...

```{r fig.width=5, fig.height=2.5, echo=FALSE}
set.seed(1)
.idx <- sample(1:nrow(.df), 500, replace=TRUE)
.df.0 <- .df[.idx, ]
.idx <- sample(1:nrow(.df), 500, replace=TRUE, prob = .df$w)
.df.bootstrap <- .df[.idx, ]

p1 <-
    ggplot(.df, aes(x,y,fill=x,group=x))+
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    geom_violin(alpha=.5, linewidth=0) +
    geom_boxplot(width = .3, outlier.size=0, outlier.stroke=0, fill="white") +
    ylab("observed outcome") + xlab("treatment") +
    ggpubr::stat_compare_means(vjust=1, hjust=0, size=3)
p2 <-
    ggplot(.df.bootstrap, aes(x,y,fill=x,group=x))+
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    geom_violin(alpha=.5, linewidth=0) +
    geom_boxplot(width = .3, outlier.size=0, outlier.stroke=0, fill="white") +
    ylab("resampled by IPW") + xlab("treatment") +
    ggpubr::stat_compare_means(vjust=1, hjust=0, size=3)
p1 | p2
```

## Key question: multiple sources of variation

- Can we identify multiple independent disease mechanisms?

- How do they manifest in observed transcriptional profiles?

\vspace{0.3cm}

1. **ER status**: Tumour-intrinsic differences (ER+ vs ER-)
2. **Age**: age effects in general population
3. **Menopause**: pre- vs. post-menopause

\vspace{0.3cm}

They are all correlated... but not necessarily the same

* Post-menopausal but young (e.g., surgical menopause)
* Pre-menopausal but older (late menopause)

```{r download-data}
data.dir <- "../data/recount3"
```

## A probabilistic model on gene expression $Y$

:::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=.45}

\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[
    node distance=1.5cm,
    observed/.style={circle, draw, fill=gray!15, minimum size=1.3cm}
]
\node[observed] (age) {Age};
\node[observed, below=1.5cm of age] (meno) {Meno};
\node[observed, below=1.5cm of meno] (er) {ER};
\node[observed, right=2.5cm of meno] (expr) {$Y_{g}$};

\draw[->, thick] (age) -- node[above] {$\beta_1$} (expr);
\draw[->, thick] (meno) -- node[above] {$\beta_2$} (expr);
\draw[->, thick] (er) -- node[below] {$\beta_3$} (expr);
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

:::
::: {.column width=.55}

**Linear model for gene $g$:**

$$Y_{ig} = \beta_{1g} \cdot X_{i1} + \beta_{2g} \cdot X_{i2} + \beta_{3g} \cdot X_{i3} + \epsilon_{ig}$$

where $\epsilon_{ig} \sim N(0, \sigma^2_g)$

\vspace{0.3cm}

* $X_{i1}$: Age for individual $i$
* $X_{i2}$: Menopause status for individual $i$
* $X_{i3}$: ER status for individual $i$
* $\beta_{1g}, \beta_{2g}, \beta_{3g}$: Coefficients for gene $g$

:::
::::::

\begin{tikzpicture}[

]

\draw[->, thick] (age) -- (expr);

\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

```{r clinical-data, echo=FALSE}
clinical <-
    colData(rse) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    select(
        age = tcga.gdc_cases.diagnoses.age_at_diagnosis,
        menopause = tcga.xml_menopause_status,
        ER.status = tcga.xml_breast_carcinoma_estrogen_receptor_status
    ) %>%
    mutate(age = age / 365.25,
           menopause = case_when(
               grepl("^Pre", menopause) ~ "Pre",
               grepl("^Peri", menopause) ~ "Peri",
               grepl("^Post", menopause) ~ "Post",
               TRUE ~ NA_character_
           ))
```

```{r confounding-data, include=FALSE}
.file <- file.path(data.dir, "lect07_er_stage_adjusted_vs_unadjusted.rds")

if.needed(.file, {
    # Prepare clinical data with sample IDs
    clinical_full <- colData(rse) %>%
        as.data.frame() %>%
        mutate(
            sample_id = rownames(.),
            age = tcga.gdc_cases.diagnoses.age_at_diagnosis / 365.25,
            menopause = case_when(
                grepl("^Pre", tcga.xml_menopause_status) ~ "Pre",
                grepl("^Peri", tcga.xml_menopause_status) ~ "Peri",
                grepl("^Post", tcga.xml_menopause_status) ~ "Post",
                TRUE ~ NA_character_
            ),
            tumour.stage = case_when(
                grepl("stage i$|stage ia|stage ib", tcga.gdc_cases.diagnoses.tumor_stage) ~ 1,
                grepl("stage ii", tcga.gdc_cases.diagnoses.tumor_stage) ~ 2,
                grepl("stage iii", tcga.gdc_cases.diagnoses.tumor_stage) ~ 3,
                grepl("stage iv", tcga.gdc_cases.diagnoses.tumor_stage) ~ 4,
                TRUE ~ NA_real_
            ),
            ER.status = tcga.xml_breast_carcinoma_estrogen_receptor_status
        ) %>%
        filter(!is.na(menopause) & !is.na(age) & !is.na(tumour.stage) &
               ER.status %in% c("Positive", "Negative"))

    counts_subset <- assay(rse, "raw_counts")[, clinical_full$sample_id]
    dge <- DGEList(counts = counts_subset)
    keep <- filterByExpr(dge)
    dge <- dge[keep, , keep.lib.sizes = FALSE]
    dge <- calcNormFactors(dge)

    # Gene symbol lookup
    gene_symbols <- rowData(rse)$gene_name[match(rownames(dge), rownames(rse))]

    # ER models
    design_er1 <- model.matrix(~ ER.status, data = clinical_full)
    design_er2 <- model.matrix(~ ER.status + age + menopause, data = clinical_full)
    fit_er1 <- eBayes(lmFit(voom(dge, design_er1, plot=FALSE), design_er1))
    fit_er2 <- eBayes(lmFit(voom(dge, design_er2, plot=FALSE), design_er2))

    # Extract ER results with adjusted p-values
    tt_er1 <- topTable(fit_er1, coef = "ER.statusPositive", number = Inf, sort.by = "none")
    tt_er2 <- topTable(fit_er2, coef = "ER.statusPositive", number = Inf, sort.by = "none")

    # Stage models
    design_st1 <- model.matrix(~ tumour.stage, data = clinical_full)
    design_st2 <- model.matrix(~ tumour.stage + age + menopause + ER.status, data = clinical_full)
    fit_st1 <- eBayes(lmFit(voom(dge, design_st1, plot=FALSE), design_st1))
    fit_st2 <- eBayes(lmFit(voom(dge, design_st2, plot=FALSE), design_st2))

    # Extract stage results with adjusted p-values
    tt_st1 <- topTable(fit_st1, coef = "tumour.stage", number = Inf, sort.by = "none")
    tt_st2 <- topTable(fit_st2, coef = "tumour.stage", number = Inf, sort.by = "none")

    results <- list(
        er = data.frame(
            gene = rownames(fit_er1$coefficients),
            symbol = gene_symbols,
            unadj = fit_er1$coefficients[, "ER.statusPositive"],
            adj = fit_er2$coefficients[, "ER.statusPositive"],
            t_unadj = fit_er1$t[, "ER.statusPositive"],
            t_adj = fit_er2$t[, "ER.statusPositive"],
            pval_unadj = tt_er1$P.Value,
            pval_adj = tt_er2$P.Value,
            padj_unadj = tt_er1$adj.P.Val,
            padj_adj = tt_er2$adj.P.Val
        ),
        stage = data.frame(
            gene = rownames(fit_st1$coefficients),
            symbol = gene_symbols,
            unadj = fit_st1$coefficients[, "tumour.stage"],
            adj = fit_st2$coefficients[, "tumour.stage"],
            t_unadj = fit_st1$t[, "tumour.stage"],
            t_adj = fit_st2$t[, "tumour.stage"],
            pval_unadj = tt_st1$P.Value,
            pval_adj = tt_st2$P.Value,
            padj_unadj = tt_st1$adj.P.Val,
            padj_adj = tt_st2$adj.P.Val
        ),
        clinical_full = clinical_full,
        dge = dge,
        gene_symbols = gene_symbols
    )
    saveRDS(results, .file)
})

results <- readRDS(.file)
```

## ER effect: with vs. without adjustment

:::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=.5}

**Unadjusted:**
$$Y_g \sim \text{ER}$$

**Adjusted:**
$$Y_g \sim \text{ER} + \text{Age} + \text{Meno}$$

:::

## Tumour stage effect: with vs. without adjustment

:::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=.5}

**Unadjusted:**
$$Y_g \sim \text{Stage}$$

**Adjusted:**

```{r stage-prep, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Identify genes that gained significance after adjustment
# (not significant before, significant after)
results$stage <- results$stage %>%
    mutate(
        effect_change = abs(adj - unadj),
        gained_sig = (padj_unadj >= 0.05) & (padj_adj < 0.05)
    )

# Top 3 genes that gained significance, sorted by effect change
gained_genes <- results$stage %>%
    filter(gained_sig) %>%
    arrange(desc(effect_change)) %>%
    head(3) %>%
    pull(gene)

# Top 3 most significant genes after adjustment
top_sig_genes <- results$stage %>%
    arrange(padj_adj) %>%
    head(3) %>%
    pull(gene)

results$stage <- results$stage %>%
    mutate(
        highlight_gained = gene %in% gained_genes,
        highlight_top = gene %in% top_sig_genes
    )
```

**Observed confounders:** Age, Meno, ER

* Can be measured and adjusted

\vspace{0.3cm}

**Unobserved confounders:** $U$

* Batch effects, sample quality
* Stromal/immune cell contamination
* Technical artifacts
* Cannot directly measure $\rightarrow$ estimate via PCA/RUV

## SBSN promotes tumour endothelial migration and therapy resistance

:::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=.5}

**Expression in Breast Cancer:**

* Upregulated in tumour endothelial cells (TEC) vs. normal endothelial cells [@Alam2014-ic]

* Induced by radio- or chemotherapy in breast cancer cell lines

* Elevated in cancer stem-like cells with low-adhesive phenotype

:::
::: {.column width=.5}

**Function:**

* Promotes migration and tube formation in TEC

* Activates AKT signaling pathway

* Involved in therapy resistance and anoikis resistance

* Associated with poor prognosis in multiple cancers [@Tan2022-ta]

:::
::::::

## COL19A1 loss marks basement membrane invasion

:::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=.5}

**Loss during invasion:**

* Completely absent in invasive breast carcinomas [@Amenta2003-pe]

* Loss precedes basement membrane invasion

* Occurs earlier than type IV collagen and laminin loss

* Signals ECM remodelling to promote tumour infiltration

:::
::: {.column width=.5}

**Anti-tumour NC1 domain:**

* NC1 domain inhibits tumour cell migration and invasion [@Oudart2016-mi]

* Works through integrin αvβ3 receptor

* Inhibits FAK/PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway

* Anti-angiogenic properties

* Plasmin cleavage releases protective fragments

:::
::::::

## Did we capture all the confounding effects?

\large

What if we have unmeasured confounding variables?

* **A solution** (`lect09`): \textbf{\color{teal} Principal Component Analysis} [@Hotelling1933-yr; @Jolliffe1986-ik]

\vfill

* PCA decomposes total variance of a matrix into independent components.

\normalsize

```{r pc-compute, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
.file <- file.path(data.dir, "pc_analysis_results.rds")

if.needed(.file, {
    ## Get the same clinical data and DGE from confounding-data chunk
    ## by loading the saved results which contains dge, clinical_full, gene_symbols
    conf_results <- readRDS(file.path(data.dir, "lect07_er_stage_adjusted_vs_unadjusted.rds"))

    clinical_full <- conf_results$clinical_full
    dge <- conf_results$dge
    gene_symbols <- conf_results$gene_symbols

    ## Compute log-CPM for PCA
    logcpm <- cpm(dge, log = TRUE)

    ## Perform PCA on genes (rows) - transpose so samples are rows
    ## Scale to give all genes equal variance
    pca_res <- prcomp(t(logcpm), scale. = TRUE, center = TRUE)

    ## Extract top 5 PCs
    top_pcs <- pca_res$x[, 1:5]
    colnames(top_pcs) <- c("PC1", "PC2", "PC3", "PC4", "PC5")

    ## Get additional clinical covariates from original rse
    clinical_extra <- colData(rse)[clinical_full$sample_id, ] %>%
        as.data.frame() %>%
        select(PR = tcga.xml_breast_carcinoma_progesterone_receptor_status,
               HER2 = tcga.xml_her2_immunohistochemistry_level_result,
               Grade = tcga.xml_neoplasm_histologic_grade)

    ## Add PCs to clinical data
    clinical_pc <- clinical_full %>%
        bind_cols(clinical_extra) %>%
        mutate(PC1 = top_pcs[, "PC1"],
               PC2 = top_pcs[, "PC2"],
               PC3 = top_pcs[, "PC3"],
               PC4 = top_pcs[, "PC4"],
               PC5 = top_pcs[, "PC5"])

    ## Compute variance explained
    var_explained <- summary(pca_res)$importance[2, 1:5] * 100

    ## Store results
    pc_data <- list(
        pcs = top_pcs,
        clinical_pc = clinical_pc,
        var_explained = var_explained,
        dge = dge,
        gene_symbols = gene_symbols
    )
    saveRDS(pc_data, .file)
})

pc_data <- readRDS(.file)
```

## Tumour stage effect: with vs. without PC adjustment

:::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=.5}

**Model 1 (with known covariates):**
$$Y_g \sim \text{Stage} + \text{Age} + \text{Meno} + \text{ER}$$

**Model 2 (with PCs added):**
$$Y_g \sim \text{Stage} + \text{Age} + \text{Meno} + \text{ER} + \text{PC1-5}$$

:::
::: {.column width=.5}

```{r pc-analysis, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
.file <- file.path(data.dir, "pc_limma_results.rds")
if.needed(.file, {
    dge <- pc_data$dge
    clinical_pc <- pc_data$clinical_pc
    gene_symbols <- pc_data$gene_symbols

    ## Model without PCs (same as before)
    design_st_base <- model.matrix(~ tumour.stage + age + menopause + ER.status,
                                   data = clinical_pc)

    ## Model with PCs
    design_st_pc <- model.matrix(~ tumour.stage + age + menopause + ER.status +
                                   PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5,
                                 data = clinical_pc)

    ## Fit models
    fit_st_base <- eBayes(lmFit(voom(dge, design_st_base, plot=FALSE), design_st_base))
    fit_st_pc <- eBayes(lmFit(voom(dge, design_st_pc, plot=FALSE), design_st_pc))

    ## Extract results
    tt_st_base <- topTable(fit_st_base, coef = "tumour.stage", number = Inf, sort.by = "none")
    tt_st_pc <- topTable(fit_st_pc, coef = "tumour.stage", number = Inf, sort.by = "none")

    results_pc <- data.frame(
        gene = rownames(fit_st_base$coefficients),
        symbol = gene_symbols,
        base = fit_st_base$coefficients[, "tumour.stage"],
        with_pc = fit_st_pc$coefficients[, "tumour.stage"],
        t_base = fit_st_base$t[, "tumour.stage"],
        t_pc = fit_st_pc$t[, "tumour.stage"],
        pval_base = tt_st_base$P.Value,
        pval_pc = tt_st_pc$P.Value,
        padj_base = tt_st_base$adj.P.Val,
        padj_pc = tt_st_pc$adj.P.Val
    )
    saveRDS(results_pc, .file)
})
results_pc <- readRDS(.file)
```

```{r pc-prep, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
## Identify genes that changed after PC adjustment
results_pc <- results_pc %>%
    mutate(
        effect_change = abs(with_pc - base),
        gained_sig = (padj_base >= 0.05) & (padj_pc < 0.05),
        lost_sig = (padj_base < 0.05) & (padj_pc >= 0.05)
    )

## Top genes that gained significance
gained_pc_genes <- results_pc %>%
    filter(gained_sig) %>%
    arrange(desc(effect_change)) %>%
    head(3) %>%
    pull(gene)

## Top genes that lost significance
lost_pc_genes <- results_pc %>%
    filter(lost_sig) %>%
    arrange(desc(effect_change)) %>%
    head(3) %>%
    pull(gene)

results_pc <- results_pc %>%
    mutate(
        highlight_gained = gene %in% gained_pc_genes,
        highlight_lost = gene %in% lost_pc_genes
    )
```

## GLYAT: potential confounding via stromal contamination

* Liver and kidney-specific metabolic enzyme [@Matsuo2012-xs]

* Predominantly expressed in stromal cells, not tumour cells [@Xia2024-ap]

* Downregulated in liver and renal cancers

## ADH4: potential confounding via hormonal regulation

* Class II alcohol dehydrogenase, primarily liver-expressed [@Jelski2006-zb]

* Regulated by steroid hormones (estrogen) [@Qulali1992-xg]

* Class I ADH dramatically reduced in invasive breast cancer [@Triano2003-bq]

## PGM5 regulates cancer cell proliferation and invasion

* Phosphoglucomutase catalyzes interconversion of glucose-1-phosphate and glucose-6-phosphate

* Key enzyme in glucose metabolism pathway

* Downregulated in colorectal cancer tissues [@Sun2019-vr]

* Low PGM5 expression associated with poor overall survival

* Overexpression inhibits proliferation, invasion and migration

* Independent prognostic factor for overall survival

## ADGRA2 linked to chemotherapy resistance

:::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=.5}

**Breast Cancer Evidence:**

* Amplified at 8p11.23 in NAC non-responsive tumours [@Yin2024-zv]

* Novel biomarker for chemotherapy resistance

* Associated with poor prognosis

* Overexpressed in breast cancer stem cells

:::
::: {.column width=.5}

**General Cancer Role:**

* Originally identified as tumour endothelial marker 5 (TEM5)

* Implicated in migration, proliferation, survival

* Involved in angiogenesis, invasion, metastasis

* Linked to gefitinib resistance in lung cancer

:::
::::::

# Removing Unwanted Variation in RNA-seq

## Remove Unwanted Variation [@Risso2014-sa]

:::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=.7}

\large

* RUV uses factorization to estimate unwanted variation

* Control genes or negative control samples

* `RUVSeq` Bioconductor package:
  - RUVg: uses negative control genes
  - RUVs: uses replicate/negative control samples
  - RUVr: uses residuals from first-pass GLM

\normalsize

:::
::: {.column width=.3}

\vspace{1cm}

```{r ruv-analysis, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
.file <- file.path(data.dir, "ruv_analysis_results.rds")

if.needed(.file, {
    ## Load PC analysis results to get the same data
    pc_data <- readRDS(file.path(data.dir, "pc_analysis_results.rds"))

    dge <- pc_data$dge
    clinical_pc <- pc_data$clinical_pc

    ## Get gene symbols from rse (properly named)
    gene_info <- rowData(rse)[, "gene_name", drop = FALSE]
    gene_symbols <- setNames(gene_info$gene_name, rownames(gene_info))

    ## Get counts matrix
    counts <- dge$counts

    ## Create design matrix for tumor stage (base model)
    design_base <- model.matrix(~ tumour.stage + age + menopause + ER.status,
                                 data = clinical_pc)

    ## Fit first-pass model to get residuals
    y <- DGEList(counts = counts)
    y <- calcNormFactors(y)
    y <- estimateDisp(y, design_base)
    fit_base <- glmFit(y, design_base)

    ## Use RUVr: estimate unwanted variation from residuals
    ## Use 5 factors to match PC analysis
    set.seed(123)
    ruv_result <- RUVr(counts, cIdx = 1:nrow(counts), k = 5,
                       residuals = residuals(fit_base, type = "deviance"))

    ## Extract RUV factors (W matrix)
    ruv_factors <- ruv_result$W
    colnames(ruv_factors) <- paste0("W", 1:5)

    ## Add RUV factors to clinical data
    clinical_ruv <- clinical_pc %>%
        mutate(W1 = ruv_factors[, "W1"],
               W2 = ruv_factors[, "W2"],
               W3 = ruv_factors[, "W3"],
               W4 = ruv_factors[, "W4"],
               W5 = ruv_factors[, "W5"])

    ## Fit model with RUV adjustment
    design_ruv <- model.matrix(~ tumour.stage + age + menopause + ER.status +
                                W1 + W2 + W3 + W4 + W5,
                                data = clinical_ruv)

    ## Run limma voom with RUV factors
    v_ruv <- voom(y, design_ruv, plot = FALSE)
    fit_ruv <- lmFit(v_ruv, design_ruv)
    fit_ruv <- eBayes(fit_ruv)

    ## Also run without RUV for comparison (same as base model from PC analysis)
    v_base <- voom(y, design_base, plot = FALSE)
    fit_base_limma <- lmFit(v_base, design_base)
    fit_base_limma <- eBayes(fit_base_limma)

    ## Extract results for tumor stage coefficient
    results_ruv <- data.frame(
        gene = rownames(fit_ruv),
        symbol = gene_symbols[rownames(fit_ruv)],
        base = fit_base_limma$coefficients[, "tumour.stage"],
        with_ruv = fit_ruv$coefficients[, "tumour.stage"],
        pval_base = fit_base_limma$p.value[, "tumour.stage"],
        pval_ruv = fit_ruv$p.value[, "tumour.stage"],
        t_base = fit_base_limma$t[, "tumour.stage"],
        t_ruv = fit_ruv$t[, "tumour.stage"],
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    ## Adjust p-values
    results_ruv$padj_base <- p.adjust(results_ruv$pval_base, method = "BH")
    results_ruv$padj_ruv <- p.adjust(results_ruv$pval_ruv, method = "BH")

    ## Identify genes that gained or lost significance
    results_ruv <- results_ruv %>%
        mutate(
            gained_sig = (padj_base >= 0.05) & (padj_ruv < 0.05),
            lost_sig = (padj_base < 0.05) & (padj_ruv >= 0.05)
        )

    ## Save results
    ruv_data <- list(
        results = results_ruv,
        ruv_factors = ruv_factors,
        clinical_ruv = clinical_ruv
    )
    saveRDS(ruv_data, .file)
})

ruv_data <- readRDS(.file)
results_ruv <- na.omit(ruv_data$results)
```

## Tumour stage effect: RUV adjustment

:::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=.5}

**Base model:**
$$Y_g \sim \text{Stage} + \text{Age} + \text{Meno} + \text{ER}$$

**RUV-adjusted:**
$$Y_g \sim \text{Stage} + \text{Age} + \text{Meno} + \text{ER} + W_1 + \cdots + W_5$$

:::
::: {.column width=.5}

:::
::::::


```{r include=F}
## Prepare highlighting
## Keep top 3 genes found by PCA
pca_genes <- results_ruv %>%
    filter(gene %in% gained_pc_genes) %>%
    head(3) %>%
    pull(gene)

## Find top 3 additional genes found by RUV (not in PCA genes)
additional_ruv_genes <- results_ruv %>%
    filter(gained_sig, !gene %in% gained_pc_genes) %>%
    arrange(padj_ruv) %>%
    head(3) %>%
    pull(gene)

## Combine PCA genes and additional RUV genes
gained_genes_ruv <- c(pca_genes, additional_ruv_genes)

lost_genes_ruv <- results_ruv %>%
    filter(lost_sig) %>%
    arrange(padj_base) %>%
    head(3) %>%
    pull(gene)

## Literature examples (potentially confounded genes)
literature_genes <- results_ruv %>%
    filter(symbol %in% c("GLYAT", "ADH4")) %>%
    pull(gene)

results_ruv <- results_ruv %>%
    mutate(
        highlight_gained = gene %in% gained_genes_ruv,
        highlight_lost = gene %in% lost_genes_ruv,
        highlight_ruv_specific = gene %in% additional_ruv_genes,
        highlight_literature = gene %in% literature_genes
    )
```

## RUV adjustment: volcano plots

:::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=.5}

```{r ruv-volcano-base, echo=FALSE, fig.width=3, fig.height=2.9, onslide.plot="1-"}
ggplot(results_ruv, aes(x = base, y = -log10(padj_base)))+
    ggrastr::rasterize(geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.5, colour = "gray50"), dpi = 300) +
    geom_point(data = filter(results_ruv, highlight_gained & !highlight_ruv_specific),
               colour = "magenta", size = 2) +
    geom_point(data = filter(results_ruv, highlight_ruv_specific),
               colour = "blue", size = 2) +
    geom_point(data = filter(results_ruv, highlight_lost),
               colour = "orange", size = 2) +
    geom_point(data = filter(results_ruv, highlight_literature),
               colour = "darkgreen", size = 2) +
    geom_text_repel(data = filter(results_ruv, highlight_gained & !highlight_ruv_specific),
                    aes(label = symbol), size = 2.2, colour = "magenta",
                    fontface = "bold", max.overlaps = 20) +
    geom_text_repel(data = filter(results_ruv, highlight_ruv_specific),
                    aes(label = symbol), size = 2.2, colour = "blue",
                    fontface = "bold", max.overlaps = 20) +
    geom_text_repel(data = filter(results_ruv, highlight_lost),
                    aes(label = symbol), size = 2.2, colour = "orange",
                    fontface = "bold", max.overlaps = 20) +
    geom_text_repel(data = filter(results_ruv, highlight_literature),
                    aes(label = symbol), size = 2.2, colour = "darkgreen",
                    fontface = "bold", max.overlaps = 20) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
    labs(x = "logFC (base)", y = "-log10(padj)", title = "Without RUV") +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10))
```

\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[
    node distance=1.2cm,
    observed/.style={circle, draw, fill=gray!15, minimum size=1cm, font=\small},
    latent/.style={circle, draw, dashed, minimum size=1cm, font=\small}
]
\node[observed] (age) {Age};
\node[observed, right=1cm of age] (meno) {Meno};
\node[observed, right=1cm of meno] (er) {ER};
\node[latent, right=1cm of er] (u) {$U$};
\node[latent, right=1cm of u] (w) {$W$};
\node[observed, below=1.5cm of meno] (stage) {Stage};
\node[observed, below=1.5cm of er] (expr) {$Y_{g}$};

\draw[->, very thick] (age) -- (stage);
\draw[->, very thick] (meno) -- (stage);
\draw[->, very thick] (er) -- (stage);
\draw[->, very thick] (age) -- (expr);
\draw[->, very thick] (meno) -- (expr);
\draw[->, very thick] (er) -- (expr);
\draw[->, very thick, dashed] (u) -- (stage);
\draw[->, very thick, dashed] (u) -- (expr);
\draw[->, very thick, dashed, blue] (w) -- (expr);
\draw[->, very thick, magenta] (stage) -- (expr);
\end{tikzpicture}
